blocks.text: The previous Messages API topic established that Anthropic's system prompt lives outside the messages array, as its own dedicated parameter, this topic goes deeper into exactly how that parameter works: its plain-string and block-array forms, how it interacts with prompt caching, and what actually belongs inside it, applying the general system prompt design principles from the earlier module concretely to Anthropic's own API.

This topic covers the plain string form, the more advanced array-of-blocks form, marking a system block for prompt caching, why system content is resent fresh on every call, what content genuinely belongs in it, and how this placement compares across providers.
1. A Dedicated Parameter, Not a Message

blocks.alt: The system parameter is applied fresh to every call, while the messages array carries the actual conversation history

blocks.text: The messages array carries the genuine back-and-forth exchange, covered in the Messages API topic, while system exists entirely separately, describing how the model should behave throughout the conversation rather than being one turn within it.
2. The Plain String Form

blocks.alt: The common case: system set to a single plain string of instructions

blocks.text: In its simplest and most common form, system is just a plain string, applying exactly the persona, tone, and scope-setting principles covered generally in the System Prompt Design module.

code.content:
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022",
    max_tokens=1024,
    system="You are a concise, technical customer support assistant for a cloud storage product.",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why did my upload fail?"}],
)

blocks.text: 2. The Array of Blocks Form

blocks.alt: A more advanced form: system as an array of separate content blocks

blocks.text: For more advanced cases, system can instead be an array of content blocks, useful when combining a persona definition with a large piece of stable reference material, a product manual or a long policy document, kept as its own separate block rather than concatenated into one string.

code.content:
system=[
    {"type": "text", "text": "You are a support assistant for a cloud storage product."},
    {"type": "text", "text": long_product_manual_text},
]

blocks.text: 3. Marking a Block for Prompt Caching

blocks.alt: A long, stable system block reused across many calls can be marked with cache_control

blocks.text: A long, unchanging block, that same product manual reused identically across thousands of separate support conversations, is exactly the case prompt caching, covered in an earlier topic, exists for. Adding cache_control to that specific block tells the provider it is safe and worthwhile to reuse the processing already done on it.

code.content:
system=[
    {"type": "text", "text": "You are a support assistant for a cloud storage product."},
    {"type": "text", "text": long_product_manual_text, "cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}},
]

blocks.text: 4. System Content Is Resent Fresh Every Call

blocks.alt: The system parameter is sent in full on every single call, there is no persistent memory of it across separate requests

blocks.text: Nothing about the system parameter persists on Anthropic's side between calls, it is resent in full every single time, which is exactly why prompt caching matters for a long, stable one, without it, the same tokens are reprocessed identically on every call in a conversation.
5. What Belongs in a System Prompt

blocks.alt: Persona, tone, and constraints belong in system; actual conversation turns never do

blocks.text: Persona, tone, scope boundaries, and output format constraints, exactly the categories covered generally in the System Prompt Design module, belong here. Genuine back-and-forth conversation, a worked example the model should treat as a real prior exchange, belongs in the messages array instead, using a few-shot style user and assistant pair, covered in the Few-Shot Prompting topic, not folded into system.
6. Length and Cost Considerations

Because system content is resent on every call in a conversation, its length directly affects the cost and latency of every single one of those calls, exactly the token cost tracking concern covered generally in an earlier module, making prompt caching's role here more than a minor optimization for any sufficiently long, stable system prompt.
7. Comparing Placement Across Providers

blocks.title: Check Every Provider Individually
blocks.content: Never assume a system prompt written for one provider's message structure will simply drop into another's request unchanged.

blocks.text: Worked Example

A team builds a customer support assistant with a system parameter made of two blocks: a short persona and scope instruction, and a long, unchanging product manual reused identically across every support conversation the assistant handles, marking only that second block with cache_control.

Across thousands of separate conversations, the persona block is small enough to reprocess cheaply every time, while the large manual block is served from the provider's cache after its first use, meaningfully lowering the cost of every conversation that follows without changing the assistant's behavior at all.
Common Mistakes

items: Assuming the system parameter persists automatically across separate, later conversations rather than being resent fresh every call
Writing an actual back-and-forth exchange inside system instead of using a real user and assistant pair in the messages array
Forgetting to mark a long, stable system block with cache_control and paying full reprocessing cost on every call
Copying a system message written for OpenAI's role-based structure directly into Anthropic's separate system parameter without adjusting the request shape

blocks.text: Practice

Build a system parameter as an array of two blocks, a short persona instruction and a longer reference passage, marking only the longer one with cache_control. Send the same request twice in a row and compare the reported token usage between the two calls.
Key Takeaway

Anthropic's system parameter can be a plain string or an array of content blocks, is resent fresh on every single call rather than persisting on its own, and should carry persona, scope, and format instructions, never actual conversation turns, with cache_control applied to any long, stable block to avoid paying full reprocessing cost repeatedly.
